test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Four word-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd one.

options.text: Sikhism : Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji

solution:
The correct answer is **__Humayun: Mughal.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad, better known by his regnal name, Humayun, **was the second emperor of the Mughal Empire, who ruled over territory in what is now Eastern Afghanistan, Pakistan, Northern India, and Bangladesh from 1530 to 1540 and again from 1555 to 1556.
 
• Humayun's most noted achievement was **in the sphere of painting**.
 
• **His devotion to the early Safavid School,** developed during his stay in Iran, led him to recruit Persian painters of merit to accompany him back to India

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gurū Nānak, also referred to as Bābā Nānak**, was the founder of Sikhism and is the first of the ten Sikh Gurus. His birth is celebrated worldwide as Guru Nanak Gurpurab on Katak Pooranmashi, i.e. October–November
 
• **Mahavira also known as Vardhamana, was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism**. He was the spiritual successor of the 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha. Mahavira was born in the early part of the 6th century BCE into a royal Kshatriya Jain family in ancient India
 
• **Gautama Buddha **was an ascetic and spiritual teacher of ancient India **who lived during the 6th or 5th century BCE. He was the founder of Buddhism** and is revered by Buddhists as a fully enlightened being who taught a path to Nirvana, freedom from ignorance, craving, rebirth and suffering.
